gallery.filename: Flowers and tributes for the victims of the Christchurch mosque shootings, Rolleston Avenue, Christchurch.jpg
gallery.title: File:Flowers and tributes for the victims of the Christchurch mosque shootings, Rolleston Avenue, Christchurch.jpg
gallery.source: Flowers and tributes for the victims of the Christchurch mosque shootings, Rolleston Avenue, Christchurch
gallery.description: The Christchurch mosque shootings were two consecutive terrorist mass shootings at Al Noor Mosque and the Linwood Islamic Centre in Christchurch, New Zealand, during Friday Prayer on 15 March 2019. The attacks began at the Al Noor Mosque in the suburb of Riccarton at 1:40 pm, and continued at the Linwood Islamic Centre at about 1:55 pm. Rolleston Avenue, between the Canterbury Museum and Christchurch Hospital (along the front of the Christchurch Botanic Gardens) is one of the sites where people put flowers, candles, tributes, and messages of aroha and support.

gallery.artist: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand
gallery.description: Hagley Park is the largest urban open space in Christchurch, New Zealand, and was created in 1855 by the Provincial Government. According to the government's decree at that time, Hagley Park is "reserved forever as a public park, and shall be open for the recreation and enjoyment of the public."

gallery.title: File:Christchurch Botanic Gardens in autumn.jpg
gallery.artist: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand
gallery.description: Founded in 1863 with the planting of an English oak tree, the Christchurch Botanic Gardens have grown from small beginnings to become a much-loved destination for Cantabrians and visitors alike. Over the years natural wetlands and sand dunes have been transformed into an elegantly cultivated 30 hectare park with more than 10 different gardens framed by mature trees and expansive lawns, which are mostly contained within a loop of the Avon River.
